elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 15.5 is retained unchanged: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York without reference to any rules of conflict of laws." New York is the preferred governing law, so no edit was needed and none was made.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Revised 15.6(a) now reads that a Dispute "shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, and each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts," replacing the JAMS referral; the JAMS Expedited Procedures/binding-award-and-judgment text and Sections 15.6(b)-(e) are struck in the operative text, so no residual merits arbitration survives. The carve-out in 15.6(j) is narrowed to "a temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction or other interim equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction pending resolution of a Dispute in the courts designated in Section 15.6(a)" \u2014 a customary interim-relief carve-out that preserves the exclusive merits forum. Residual non-court routes (JSC matters under 2.10, matters under 5.6, and the Program Invention expert determination in 15.6(i)) are pre-existing subject-matter mechanics retained unchanged, not new alternate merits forums created by the redline.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 15.5 keeps New York law; no Delaware, California or England and Wales law is designated. This is expected because the proposal targets the preferred level, and New York is superior to the fallback set.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Revised 15.6(a) designates the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware, California or London courts. Again expected, as the redline pursues the preferred level.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York law is retained and the merits forum is now the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with only a temporary/interim injunctive-relief carve-out in 15.6(j) that is expressly tethered back to "the courts designated in Section 15.6(a)."

The finding status "deviation" is correct on the forum: the original 15.6(a) committed every merits Dispute to JAMS arbitration with a redacted seat and panel, which fails both preferred and fallback (no accepted court forum designated anywhere), so a redline was warranted notwithstanding the compliant governing-law sentence.

Minimality holds. Only arbitration-dependent language was touched: the JAMS referral and Expedited-Procedures/award-entry text, the arbitration-only machinery in 15.6(b)-(e), and conforming references in 15.6(f) ("the arbitrators are not empowered"), 15.6(g) ("arbitration proceeding" \u2192 "Dispute") and 15.6(i) (cross-reference conformed from 15.6(c) to 15.6(a)). Favourable retained terms \u2014 the mutual punitive/exemplary damages waiver, the stay of termination effectiveness pending resolution, the English-language requirement, the JSC/Section 5.6 and Program Invention carve-outs \u2014 survive.

No dangling references detected: the 15.6(i) "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section 15.6(c)" pointer was conformed to 15.6(a), and 15.6(b)-(e) are placeholdered as "[Intentionally omitted.]" rather than renumbered, so lettering references elsewhere in the Agreement are undisturbed.

Advisory (not a failure): deletion of former 15.6(e) removes the mutual prevailing-party costs-and-fees entitlement rather than conforming it to the court forum. It was arbitrator-specific ("The arbitrators may award..."), so removal is defensible, but if the team wants to keep that remedy it should be re-cast as "The court may award the prevailing Party its reasonable costs and attorneys' fees" instead of struck.

Advisory (not a failure): confirm no other section of the Agreement (e.g., indemnification, escalation, or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement) cross-refers to "arbitration under Section 15.6" or to Sections 15.6(b)-(e); any such reference must be conformed to the court-jurisdiction language. Section 15.6(h) (foreign patent/trademark validity carve-out) was not rendered \u2014 verify it survives unchanged and does not reference the arbitrators.

Fallback level is deliberately unmet and that is acceptable: the preferred checklist is fully satisfied, and moving to Delaware/California/England would be a downgrade from the retained New York position.
